The latest version, i updated on tuesday thanks! How many bytes is each gas ? gas doesn't reference bytes. it's an internal measure the EVM uses to assign costs to specific computation / operations. for example, a "simple send" of ETH from one address to another costs 21,000 gas this gets multiplied by each transactions associated baseFee + priorityFee per gas (aka tip) resulting in the total tx cost in ETH / $ baseFee and priorityFee fluctuate according to congestion (pls anyone correct me if I'm wrong here) It is mainly to cover the three resources used in a transaction (Bandwidth, computational power, and storage) so a transfer might consume 2,000,000 gas due to computational power or bandwidth but store too little, I think a regular ETH transfer consumes the most storage with respect to its gas, smart contracts fees are mostly spent on computational power, so i think the best way to calculate an approximate of the maximum storage is by calculating how many many bytes each regular ETH transfer costs and multiply that by how many are possible in one block (block size limit / 21000) (Someone please correct me if i'm thinking wrong) If your goal is to burn storage, there are much more efficient ways than ETH transfers. I wanna calculate the max possible size of a block from its gas limit What do you mean by size? Biggest increase in state? size in megabytes or bytes Something like gas limit divided by 16 I think? of the block 30000000/16 bytes that gives the result in bytes ? https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/672059911034634243/880024942278762526 result is in bytes or bits ? cause this is 1,875,000 bytes Bytes. Sounds about right. ok yes 1.8 MB i was lost in calculation i forgot KB comes before MB so my end result was 1.8 GB <@683653554631868440> curious if you or anyone found some successful transaction from the responsible today. Was there actually an intent to double spend or was it only to disrupt the network? This incident shows it's pretty hard to fix a bug in open source projects and announce the release in advance and make it public. I wonder if no fuzz were made about this release what would have happened. In principle it could be much worse if people didn't care to upgrade I think it was malicious. And there did look to be a pump-and-dump during the event, but I didn't manage to track it down. I think <@!211091239112671234> is writing a post-mortem. And yeah, coordinating upgrades is especially hard when out-of-sync clients can break consensus. That it was malicious is clear as the code of that contract is only to trigger the bug. But I can imagine that they didn't get anything from it if all exchanges were upgraded I lean towards it being a griefer. It could be different actors, but it seems that some form of this transaction has been ran on most EVM chains https://twitter.com/mhswende/status/1431350139386540033 We've done silent patches (official policy: https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/vulnerabilities/vulnerabilities ) -- but doing a silent patch means 3-4-6 weeks of anticipation: "are enough upgraded yet? anyone found it yet?". It can go really really bad. And no matter what path we choose, you can be sure we'll be blamed I'm not 1000% sure I found the right bug but looking at the portion of the diff between .8 and .7 related to the evm interpreter that changed I wouldn't say it's that hard to find I skimmed it last week and figured it'd have *something* to do with what I saw but I didn't bother looking deeper until this morning trying hard to get people to upgrade was a good choice Yeah I feel for you, I can see it's a lose-lose situation but seeing "oh look they changed something very specific about the VM interpreter I wonder what that's about" in the diff even without knowing there's a vuln could be a huge hint to look for a vuln maybe if the patch was hidden in a larger refactor that would have bought more time Yeah, but going from "something related to memory" to the specific exploit was, in this case, not trivial. I promise you. I even triaged it on a very _very_ good evm hacker. We'll publish a writeup later. In this case, it took from tuesday morning to friday afternoon, which I guess was enough (but I had thought it would be more) And it was. But the patch had to be applied to Erigon and lots of other projects, which in some cases couldn't take the whole PR, but just the actual patch, so that made it easier for an astute observer to narrow it down that's a good point One thing that is helpful here is that there's not typically a large overlap between people who understand the core client + EVM well and those that want to cause a chain split One would hope so. OTOH, if one is a bit paranoid, there could very well be competitive projects who'd like nothing more than grief ethereum. And a miner could very well want to 'derail' other miners. If one were paranoid, which I'm not did this vuln also get triggered on bsc? I'd like to see the fuzz test that was written that discovered this too I believe so interesting, not surprising is there ports of parity/nethermind for bsc or are they *just* geth? Afaik just geth, but I don't really know much about bsc. Other than that bsc-users often mis-file tickets against go-ethereum well that sucks lol I believe that bsc disclosed the fix that fixed the vuln when they shouldn't have: <link hidden> why link hidden? in case someone malicious was lurking in here, idk link is https://github.com/binance-chain/bsc/releases/tag/v1.1.2 The exploit has been dissected over twitter and telegram, and exploited on several chains already but my point is that that was released before it was exploited Nah that was fine, we did release/announce it days in advance oh, ok what are those changes to the bit manipulation code do? I thought that might have also had something to do with the vuln but I didn't see a connection I just checked, I am on: ``` docker run --rm -ti ethereum/client-go version Geth Version: 1.10.9-unstable Git Commit: ea4bc2dbff949932050994d5213d9a41cf4cd6ee Architecture: amd64 Go Version: go1.16.7 Operating System: linux GOPATH= GOROOT=go ``` No idea why it is at 1.10.9 this is the commit it pulled from btw https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/commit/ea4bc2dbff949932050994d5213d9a41cf4cd6ee I forgot to add :stable to the docker pull, will update watchtheburn to that now
